name: Kelvex Transit Maintenance Ground Kit
description: The standard layered rig for MagRail ground maintenance crews who work the underbelly of the transit system — crawl spaces, signal relay stations, and track-level inspection walks. The outer shell is a waist-length hi-vis jacket in deep navy with broad reflective tape bands at the chest, waist, and cuffs, Kelvex Transit Authority logo printed in white on the left breast, and a rear panel that reads MAINTENANCE in tall retroreflective lettering. The jacket has a rear hem vent and a dorsal seam split to accommodate spinal aug rigs without bunching. Beneath it, a heavy-duty navy work shirt with a mandarin collar, hidden snap placket, and elbow patches in gunmetal grey synth-leather. Trousers are Goretek HaulMaster-style in charcoal canvas with double-layered seat and knees, cargo pockets on both thighs secured with hook-and-loop, and a tool loop array at the right hip. Steel-toe boots in matte black with a non-conductive sole and ankle-height lacing system with a secondary magnetic snap keeper. A navy knit watch cap completes the look, often pulled low.
functionality: dorsal seam split for spinal aug rigs, retroreflective hi-vis banding, non-conductive steel-toe boot, tool loop array, cargo thigh pockets, snap-placket shirt for fast layering changes, BCI-compatible sleeve cuff opening
what_it_says: Transit maintenance is unglamorous, essential work. This kit says the wearer keeps the city moving from below, unseen. The Kelvex branding marks them as employed, stable, and accountable to a schedule. Worn off-duty, it reads as honest labor — the kind of person who fixes things rather than breaks them.
manufacturer: Kelvex Transit Authority (uniform issue) / Goretek (trousers, contractor purchase)
price_range: Φ140–Φ220 (jacket and shirt employer-issued; trousers and boots personal purchase)
story_hooks: A maintenance worker discovers a section of track that has been deliberately sabotaged — and the work order log has been wiped clean.
The retroreflective lettering on the back of the jacket makes the wearer highly visible in the dark tunnels, which is a problem when they're trying to avoid the person following them.
The non-corponation trousers become a disciplinary issue when a new supervisor insists on full uniform compliance — but the issued trousers don't fit the worker's prosthetic leg.
related_entities: Ringo Heavy Transit MagRail Levitation Transport Network

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian layered ensemble presenting as a compact, purposeful silhouette. The deep navy color palette with reflective striping creates a visual hierarchy that reads as both functional and deliberately visible in transit tunnels and maintenance shafts. The overall impression is blue-collar reliability with augmentation-conscious design—professional, weathered, built for crawlspaces.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed and deliberately loose through the torso for layering and augmentation clearance. The jacket is waist-length and boxy; the work shirt drapes naturally; trousers are cut straight with a generous thigh for cargo pockets and movement in confined spaces. Everything accommodates spinal rigs without binding.
physical_description.primary_material: Navy ballistic weave jacket shell; heavy-duty cotton-blend canvas trousers; reinforced synth-leather elbow and knee patches; knit wool watch cap
physical_description.texture: The jacket has a tight, water-resistant weave with broad matte reflective tape (slightly raised, tactile striping). The work shirt is soft cotton with subtle texture variation. Canvas trousers have a broken-in, slightly napped finish. Synth-leather patches feel smooth and durable. Matte black rubber soles and steel-toe caps.
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep navy blue as dominant color; broad bands of high-visibility reflective white/silver at chest, waist, and cuffs; gunmetal grey synth-leather patches; matte black boots; white printed Kelvex logo and MAINTENANCE lettering
physical_description.closures: Jacket: full-length YKK zipper with magnetic storm flap; Work shirt: hidden snap placket (industrial-grade); Trousers: hook-and-loop cargo pocket closures, standard waist button and zip; Boots: traditional laced with secondary magnetic snap ankle keeper
distinctive_features: Rear dorsal seam split to accommodate spinal augmentation rigs
Rear panel with tall retroreflective MAINTENANCE lettering (visible in headlamp beam)
Kelvex Transit Authority logo on left breast pocket
Tool loop array on right hip (4-6 loops for wrench/socket positioning)
Double-layered seat and knee reinforcement on trousers
Non-conductive rubber sole on boots (electrical safety)
Elbow and knee patches in contrasting gunmetal synth-leather
Rear hem vent on jacket for ventilation in tunnels
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3–4 (working class/essential infrastructure). Issue uniform signals regular employment and system integration, but material quality and wear patterns reflect blue-collar functionality rather than luxury.
physical_description.cultural_context: The wearer is a transit infrastructure worker—someone who crawls through MagRail underbelly maintenance shafts, handles live equipment, and keeps the metropolitan pulse running. This outfit communicates competence, regulated employment, and comfort with industrial environments. No corpo affectation, no street hustle—pure functional authority.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in and well-maintained. The reflective tape shows minor scuffing; the synth-leather patches on elbows and knees are darkened from repeated contact with tunnel walls and crawl-space grime. The boots are regularly cleaned but retain a dull patina from non-conductive rubber wear. The work shirt collar shows faint sweat-line darkening. Everything is regulation-clean but visibly used.
